## Problem

After a reclaim publish-swap, a clone whose `origin/tickets` was already fetched to the rewritten baseline refuses every ticket write as DIVERGED, even though the remote's store epoch provably supersedes the local one and `_store/sync.py::_override_if_reclaimed` would move the clone onto the new history.

Observed 2026-11-20 PST after publishing 6a6dda16fc7: the box MCP server's first write (`comment_ticket`) failed with "ticket write refused: the local ticket store has DIVERGED from the shared store with no shared ancestor". The same write through the local CLI succeeded and the sync logged "clone moved onto reclaimed remote … replayed 0 unpushed event(s)". The MCP clone had to be reset by hand.

## Cause (reproduced)

`_commands/_seam.py::finalize_event` calls `_refuse_unpublishable_store` → `_store/freshness.py::write_blocking_divergence`, which returns `diverged` whenever `merge-base HEAD <remote>/<branch>` fails. It never consults `compat.remote_epoch_supersedes_local`, and nothing on the write path runs the stale-clone override itself.

Why the CLI write healed and the MCP write did not: a write reaches `sync.reconverge` (fetch + override) only through the read path's `reads.ensure_fresh`, which the CLI runs before every write arm and the library write runs via `emit_cross_session_warning` → `show_ticket`. That reconverge is throttled to once per 60 s by a marker file. A short-lived CLI process whose marker is old reconverges first and is moved onto the reclaimed baseline before `finalize_event` runs. A long-running MCP server that reads constantly is usually inside the 60 s window, so its write skips the reconverge and the precheck is the first code to see the already-fetched superseded ref. Reproduction in a throwaway repo with a real bare origin: with the marker stamped as just-run, `rebar.comment` refuses with DIVERGED on current main; with the marker absent, the same write succeeds. What fetched the box's ref without the override running (for example an idle-sync round that found the write lock busy, or an earlier push-recovery fetch) was not established from the box.

Rejected fix (tested): only making the precheck return `None` for a superseded clone lets the event commit on the superseded history, but it never reaches the remote. The push is rejected as non-fast-forward and `_store/push_recovery.py::_merge_remote_under_lock` tries to merge the unrelated reclaimed history (5 attempts, each "merge conflict").

## Approach

Heal the superseded clone and then compose the event on the reclaimed baseline, instead of committing on the superseded history and repairing during push. Committing first would hand the new event to the stale-clone override, which discards every unpushed event (the new one included) when the clone's oldest unpushed event predates the reclaim horizon, and it would need a second override path inside push recovery (which completion delivery also uses for private-ref merges).

The heal runs only after the existing precheck has already refused, so a healthy store pays no extra git calls on any write (the op-cert service's per-pass git-spawn ceiling test stays unchanged; a first draft that probed before every write exceeded it).

- `_store/freshness.py::write_blocking_divergence` additionally reports `superseded: true` on its `diverged` verdict when `compat.remote_epoch_supersedes_local(tracker, <remote_ref commit>)` holds. This is computed only on the path that already refuses.
- `_commands/_seam.py::_refuse_unpublishable_store` raises `SupersededStoreRefused` (a `CommandError` subclass, same message and exit code) for a superseded verdict, before anything is committed.
- New `_commands/_seam.py::retry_after_superseded_heal(write, tracker)`: run the write; on `SupersededStoreRefused`, run `_store/freshness.py::heal_superseded_clone(tracker)` and retry the write once. The heal is the existing `sync.reconverge` round: fetch, take the write lock, `_override_if_reclaimed`, which backs the tip up under `refs/rebar/stale-override/`, resets onto the reclaimed baseline and replays fresh unpushed events. It is best-effort and never raises; a second refusal propagates.
- Apply it to the writes that take and release the write lock themselves, so the heal runs with the lock free: `_seam.append_event` (wrapping composition and commit, so the retried event is composed after the clone moved), and `_commands/txn.py::transition_core` / `claim_core` through a typed `heals_superseded_store` decorator (they reduce fresh state under the lock on the retry).
- An unrelated remote (lineage does not name the local epoch), or a superseded clone the heal could not move (fetch failure, busy lock, unreadable horizon config, failed override), is still refused as DIVERGED.
- No new config key, env var or flag. `push_recovery.py` is not changed.

## Scope

In: `src/rebar/_store/freshness.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, `docs/concurrency.md`, and a new regression test module. Out: the atomic completion close (`completion_txn`, which pins the tickets OID before taking the lock), delete, reconciler-inbound and NDJSON-import/batch writes. These keep today's DIVERGED refusal on a superseded clone until a read or idle-sync round moves it; the refusal is a `CommandError` subclass, so their error handling is unchanged. A clone whose remote-tracking ref has not been fetched yet is not superseded from the write path's view; its next sync round moves it, as today. Also out: gate-read freshness (`store_freshness`) and the 60 s read throttle.

## Testing

New `tests/interfaces/store/test_write_after_reclaim.py` drives the library against a real bare origin that a parentless baseline replaced, with the read-path throttle marker stamped as just-run so the write path is the first code to see the superseded ref:
- `rebar.comment` on a clone whose remote lineage names its epoch lands on the remote tip on top of that baseline. Fails on current main with "ticket write refused … DIVERGED".
- The same with an older-than-horizon unpushed local event: the new comment still lands, and the old event is kept under the stale-override backup ref.
- `rebar.transition` open → in_progress on a superseded clone lands on the remote.
- A baseline whose lineage names another epoch is still refused as DIVERGED, with neither the clone nor the remote moved.

Existing `tests/unit/test_stale_clone_override.py`, `tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py` and `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_push_pending.py` must stay green, then `make verify`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A regression test builds a clone on epoch A, a remote rewritten to epoch B whose lineage names A, fetches the remote ref, and performs a ticket write through the shared seam: the write succeeds and the event is on the remote tip. The test fails on current main.
- [x] A remote with an unrelated history (lineage does not name the local epoch) is still refused as DIVERGED.
- [x] `make verify` passes.
